name: A boy in grey velvet, Paris
bio: A young man Wilde was seen with outside a small café behind the Madeleine in Paris in late March 1900, eight months before his death. He is known from a single sentence of Wilde's own, written to Robert Ross: Ross's brother Aleck walked past and saw them together. Wilde describes him as 'a beautiful boy in grey velvet - half rough, all Hylas' - 'rough' being the period word for a working-class young man, and Hylas the youth Herakles loved and lost. No name, age or occupation is recorded, and nothing else about him survives.
bio_note: Sole source: Wilde to Robert Ross, Thursday [Late March 1900], Grand Cafe, 14 boulevard des Capucines, Paris; Complete Letters (2000), printed 1177. The editors' footnote 3 to that page explains Wilde's joke about Aleck's eye: 'Aleck Ross had lost the sight of one eye in early youth.'
